claims.text: Israel recognized Mujama al-Islamiya as a charity, then as an association in 1979; allowed it to build schools, clinics, mosques and an Islamic university; officials said the main concern was Fatah and avoiding appearing an enemy of Islam; Israel often stayed out of Islamist–secular clashes.

Avner Cohen (religious affairs official in Gaza): 'Hamas, to my great regret, is Israel's creation'; mid-1980s he urged breaking up 'this monster'. David Hacham: 'I think we made a mistake.' Shalom Harari: failures were neglect, Israel never financed or armed Hamas. Arieh Spitzen doubted political Islam could have been curbed sooner.

Yassin arrested 1984 over a weapons cache, said the arms were for rival Palestinians, released after a year; founded Hamas in 1987 with six others; released 1997 after the failed Mossad attempt on Mashaal.
Yitzhak Segev, military governor of Gaza early 1980s: 'The Israeli government gave me a budget… and the military government gives to the mosques.'
